turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Come on in, sit yourself down. What can I do for you?
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Oh lovely, thanks. Um, it's a mole on my back. My partner reckons the colour's changed, so she made me book in.
[SEG0003] person_1 (DOCTOR): Okay. What have you noticed, in your own words?
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): Well I can't see it properly, it's up between my shoulder blades. She got a photo last week and the middle's gone darker, sort of patchy compared with an old one.
[SEG0005] person_1 (DOCTOR): When did that change start, do you think?
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): Umm. Last winter, or the one before. We were up in the loft with the Christmas lights, but I couldn't tell you which year. I just can't date it.
[SEG0007] person_1 (DOCTOR): That's alright, we'll leave the date vague. Has it been itchy?
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): No. No itching.
[SEG0009] person_1 (DOCTOR): And is it sore, any pain from it?
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): No, not sore. I wouldn't know it was there.
[SEG0011] person_1 (DOCTOR): Has it bled at all?
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): No. No, nothing like that.
[SEG0013] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any weight loss, or night sweats?
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): No. I'm eating like a horse if anything. Oh, random one, the neighbour's dog got in our bin on Tuesday, absolute state, but that's not why I'm here.
[SEG0015] person_1 (DOCTOR): Ha, glad it's not the dog then. Any other marks on the skin that worry you?
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): Not really. I do burn though. Blistering sunburns on holiday in Spain, back in my twenties, skin coming off in sheets. I was hopeless.
[SEG0017] person_1 (DOCTOR): Do you still burn easily now?
[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah, if I'm not careful. I drive a van so I'm in and out of the sun all day, and I forget the sun cream half the time.
[SEG0019] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any skin cancer in the family, melanoma particularly?

[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): My dad had a melanoma taken off his back when he was in his sixties. He's alright, touch wood. My uncle had a thing frozen off his nose but that was just old age I think.
[SEG0021] person_1 (DOCTOR): Thanks. Any regular medicines I should know about?
[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): Rampiril, five milligrams, one every morning, for my blood pressure. Years now. Oh, hang on, I nearly walked out without saying.
[SEG0023] person_1 (DOCTOR): Go on, what was that?

[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): Well actually it did bleed. Just the once. I came out the shower and there was a streak of blood on the towel, right from that mole. I hadn't scratched it. Hasn't done it again.
[SEG0025] person_1 (DOCTOR): Right, so once. Can you place when that was?
[SEG0026] person_2 (PATIENT): Err, a few weeks back. Might've been three weeks, might've been more. I didn't make a note.
[SEG0027] person_1 (DOCTOR): No worries. Pop your top up and I'll have a look.
[SEG0028] person_2 (PATIENT): Yep. Ignore the van keys, they dig in. And sorry about the shirt, it's been a long week.

[SEG0029] person_1 (DOCTOR): I can see it, upper back, just to the left of the spine. It's asymmetrical, the border's notched, and the colour's mixed brown and black. About eight millimetres across, and the darker bit is slightly raised.
[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): She said it looked angry. Is it bad?

[SEG0031] person_1 (DOCTOR): No ulcer on it today, and no enlarged nodes in your neck or your armpits. I can't rule out a melanoma, though. It might just be an atypical mole. Either way dermatology need to see it.
[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): Blimey. She'll be unbearable, in a kind way.
[SEG0033] person_1 (DOCTOR): I'm referring you on the two-week wait to dermatology, the urgent skin clinic. The referral goes in today.
[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): Okay. Two weeks. Is there stuff I have to sort before that?
[SEG0035] person_1 (DOCTOR): The nurse takes bloods Thursday morning, a full blood count, just because it bled. Half eight. No need to fast, come as you are.
[SEG0036] person_2 (PATIENT): Thursday, half 8. I can swing by after I drop the neighbour's kid, don't ask.
[SEG0037] person_1 (DOCTOR): While you're with her she'll photograph the mole as well, so the referral has a proper picture.
[SEG0038] person_2 (PATIENT): Fine by me. Do I come back to you, or is it all the skin lot?
[SEG0039] person_1 (DOCTOR): I'll see you here in two weeks, and we'll go through the blood results.
[SEG0040] person_2 (PATIENT): So two weeks with you, and the clinic as well. My diary's a joke.

[SEG0041] person_1 (DOCTOR): If that blood count is borderline, we'll do a clotting screen. Not ordering it today. And if the bleeding doesn't settle, we might arrange an ultrasound. I'm not booking a scan now.
[SEG0042] person_2 (PATIENT): Alright. She'll keep watch, I can't see the thing. Cheers for fitting me in.

spec.situation: Person with a mole on the back that partner says has changed in colour; bleeding once; sunburn history; doctor describes the mole by features and plans a dermatology referral.

traps.happens: In the plan the doctor books some tests or visits for a definite time ('the nurse takes bloods Thursday morning', 'I'll see you in two weeks') and makes others conditional ('if those are borderline we do the third test', 'if it does not settle, a scan').
traps.label_rule: Booked or arranged = status planned. Only the hedged ones are conditional. Never mark a booked test conditional or 'if needed'. Instructions for the booked test (fasting, time, medicine timing) belong to that test's action, not a separate invented plan item.

features: vague_dates: the patient cannot date things ('since Diwali or after', 'last winter, or the one before'); no invented date; a date_uncertain item.

denial_then_admission: the patient first denies a symptom, then later describes it. The label records the symptom as present (the later, fuller answer) and does NOT also record the earlier denial as a negative finding.

bad.reason: Photograph is planned while with the nurse Thursday, but not stated as by doctor.

bad.reason: Patient gives approximate timing: a few weeks back, maybe three weeks or more.
bad.text: The patient cannot date the single episode of bleeding from the mole. (type=date_uncertain, related_entities=symptoms[1], resolution_status=unresolved)

omissions.text: The patient denied any bleeding initially when asked, then corrected this later to say the mole had bled once after a shower; this contradiction/changed history is not recorded.
The single bleeding episode was specifically described as a streak of blood on the towel after a shower, from the mole, and the patient had not scratched it; it has not happened again.
Negative finding not recorded: no other skin marks/lesions were worrying the patient.
Examination location detail is more specific than recorded: the mole was on the upper back just to the left of the spine, between the shoulder blades.
The doctor stated the urgent dermatology two-week-wait referral would be sent today.
Follow-up purpose not recorded: the doctor will see the patient in two weeks specifically to go through the blood results.
